# Support matrix

Which platforms dev-fleet runs on, in which role, and what happens to the
rest. The default is one macOS manager and Ubuntu workers treated as cattle.

- **supported**: converged, measured and tested on every pull request.
- **best effort**: works and is not tested as a fleet role.
- **refused**: stopped with the named reason before anything is installed.

<!-- Generated by `bun src/machine/support-matrix.ts` from ansible/macos/policy.json, ansible/ubuntu/policy.json and ansible/platforms.json; features/rules/support-matrix.feature fails when it differs. -->

| Role           | Platform  | Versions            | Architectures   | Status      | Note                                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------- | ------------------- | --------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| manager        | macOS     | 14 or newer         | arm64, x86_64   | supported   | ansible/macos/policy.json                                                                 |
| worker         | Ubuntu    | 26.04 (resolute)    | amd64, arm64    | supported   | ansible/ubuntu/policy.json; a machine of its own, physical or virtual                     |
| manager        | any other | any                 | any             | refused     | The fleet configuration accepts only a macOS manager.                                     |
| worker         | Ubuntu    | any other release   | any             | refused     | UBUNTU_BASELINE_MISMATCH                                                                  |
| worker         | Ubuntu    | an accepted release | any other       | refused     | UBUNTU_BASELINE_MISMATCH                                                                  |
| worker         | Debian    | any                 | any             | refused     | UBUNTU_BASELINE_MISMATCH                                                                  |
| worker         | macOS     | any                 | any             | refused     | The fleet configuration accepts only Linux workers.                                       |
| worker         | Windows   | any                 | any             | refused     | The fleet configuration accepts only Linux workers.                                       |
| worker         | WSL2      | any                 | any             | refused     | WORKER_ENVIRONMENT_UNSUPPORTED                                                            |
| worker         | container | any                 | any             | refused     | WORKER_ENVIRONMENT_UNSUPPORTED                                                            |
| toolchain only | macOS     | any                 | arm64, x86_64   | best effort | No fleet role: devfleet bootstrap installs the pinned tools (docs/machine-setup.md).      |
| toolchain only | Linux     | any                 | x86_64, aarch64 | best effort | No fleet role: devfleet bootstrap installs the pinned tools (docs/machine-setup.md).      |
| toolchain only | WSL2      | any                 | x86_64          | best effort | Treated as Linux: devfleet bootstrap installs the pinned tools (docs/machine-setup.md).   |
| toolchain only | Windows   | any                 | x64             | best effort | No fleet role: bootstrap/bootstrap.ps1 installs the pinned tools (docs/machine-setup.md). |
| toolchain only | Alpine    | any                 | any             | refused     | musl: the pinned mise build needs glibc.                                                  |

A worker is refused by the first check that can tell: the fleet configuration
refuses a worker that is not Linux, the platform probe refuses another
release, CPU or environment (`ubuntu:release`, `platform:environment`), and
the bootstrap and the Ubuntu baseline refuse them again on the machine.

Supporting another platform means adding it to the policy that names it, with
its package pins, a fresh-box job and its row here.
